verdicts.why: Marvel Database files the Victor who gets the TVA handbook in 1868 as Victor Timely (Earth-TRN1071), Reality = Earth-TRN1071, played by Jonathan Majors in Quantumania and Loki S2 (the 1893 fair, the Loom, his death and his return). The Earth-199999 Victor is the Sacred Timeline boy who never gets the book. Every step on file belongs to the branched Victor, so the corrected Earth is Earth-TRN1071 (the way Sylvie's file keeps Earth-62171).

held: minor employer. Doctors Without Borders is a single past job named once in passing (the MCU Wiki lists it as 'mentioned' in S2 episode 9 'For Pete's Sake', not episode 11 as proposed), so it stays an open owner question, like Lincoln's hospital job. Until the owner decides, the record stands.

Bakuto trained in K'un-Lun, perverted its teachings with the other four Fingers, was banished, and co-founded the Hand (Stick tells it in The Defenders episode 4). That is a past group, so it goes first, keyed to his first title, Iron Fist S1. He serves the Hand in both titles, so the K'un-Lun stage at The Defenders wrongly reads as a move. Ending on the Hand is right.

Same origin, told in The Defenders episode 4: Sowande trained in K'un-Lun and was banished with the other Fingers, who formed the Hand. The past group goes first, then the Hand, which he serves until Stick kills him. The record's leading Hand stage before K'un-Lun is wrong.

The second fix holds: North kills Ayala on his own (episode 3) and first serves Fisk when Fisk recruits him into the Task Force in episode 6 'Excessive Force', so the leading Fisk's Empire stage goes. The Chicago Police Department stage does not hold. Fisk says only 'Born and raised in Chicago, top of your class in the Academy, made Detective in only three years... Yet here you are in New York', and the MCU Wiki marks the department as only 'indirectly mentioned'. Its own timeline puts the Academy and detective rank in the NYPD (2011, 2014), and Marvel Database lists only the NYPD and the Task Force. A department inferred from a home town is not a stage.

S1: Garrett was a S.H.I.E.L.D. agent under Fury, was recruited into HYDRA in 1990 after Sarajevo while keeping his cover, and ran Centipede as the Clairvoyant, so S.H.I.E.L.D. goes first. S7 episode 10 'Stolen': the young S.H.I.E.L.D. recruit joins Nathaniel Malick at the Krazy Kanoe, so Malick's Crew is the last stage. FLAG: Marvel Database files that S7 Garrett separately as Jonathan Garrett (Earth-19859), as it does Jiaying and Gordon (items 81 and 82), so his two S7 stages may belong on a separate by/Earth-19859 record.

Garrett recruited the teenage Ward into HYDRA and sent him into S.H.I.E.L.D. undercover. He works with Garrett's Centipede only after the S1 episode 17 reveal (the MCU Wiki lists Centipede Project, formerly). So Centipede comes after S.H.I.E.L.D., not before it.

held: minor employer. Rawlins Logistics Corp is his family's business, named once in his background in S1 episode 8 'Cold Steel' (the MCU Wiki lists it as 'mentioned' only). That is a single minor job, which stays an open owner question like Zelma's family shop, so the record stands for now.

held: minor employer. On screen Cal says he was in China volunteering for Doctors Without Borders and was meant to be there for two weeks. A short volunteer stint told once is a single minor job, so it stays an open owner question. (Side note: the MCU Wiki gives his current affiliation as Winslow's Veterinary Clinic, the new life he starts at the end of S2. That is another possible employer the record lacks, for the owner.)

The HYDRA part holds. In S3 episodes 18 to 22, Hive's Inhumans take Radcliffe to the town Hive bought with Malick's HYDRA money. He runs the Kree experiment on HYDRA volunteers and makes the Primitives until S.H.I.E.L.D. takes him in (Marvel Database lists Hydra, formerly), which is service and counts. GT Agrochemical is held: minor employer. It is a past lab job told once, in one Simmons line ('the agrochemical lab we raided'), so it stays an open owner question.

His file shown in S3 episode 8 gives his U.S. Marine Corps enlistment and Somalia service, and Coulson says 'Before the ATCU Giyera spent years in Special Ops'. Armed forces count. Marvel Database lists US Marines (formerly), and the dataset already uses 'U.S. Marine Corps'. As a past group it goes first, keyed to his first title.

After his S3 episode 11 arrest for corruption, Ramon is a jail escapee who says 'Me and my compañeros were the law!', so he is no longer police. In Slingshot he only steals the 0-8-4 to sell to his Watchdogs contacts, as a seller and ally, never a member. Marvel Database lists only the Colombian Police. So he ends in no group, with left set to Slingshot.

In S4 episode 20 Aida leaves the Framework for her human body, and its deletion in episodes 21 and 22 erases the Framework and its HYDRA, so the group ends. Afterwards she acts on her own, only uneasily allied with Ivanov, until Coulson kills her. So she ends in no group, with left set to S4.

Marvel Database files the 1983 Jiaying of the Chronicom-altered past separately: Jiaying (Earth-19859), Reality = Earth-19859, affiliation Afterlife, first seen S7 episode 8, killed by Nathaniel Malick in episode 10. So the episode 133 step goes to a separate by record on Earth-19859 with Afterlife (from the start), matching Kora and Nathaniel Malick. The main record keeps episodes 39 and 44.

Marvel Database files the 1983 Gordon separately: Gordon (Earth-19859), Reality = Earth-19859, base Afterlife. His history diverges in October 1983, he first appears in S7 episode 8 and dies in episode 10. So the episode 133 step goes to a by record on Earth-19859 with Afterlife (from the start). The main record keeps episodes 38 and 44.

Whitney is the studio's contract star across several S2 episodes: on set, in her dressing room, and told in 'Smoke & Mirrors' that the studio wanted to recast her. In 'Monsters' (S2 episode 7) she holds a press conference outside Anvil Studios, its name and seal on screen, and retires from acting. That makes it a real employer, not a single minor job. It goes first and ends inside S2, and the Council of Nine stays last.

In 'Shriek of the Vulture', Toomes owns his own firm, joins its board meeting by phone and fights Norman's bid to merge it into Oscorp ('He dares to take my company from me'), so his first stage is that company, the way Norman's is Oscorp. Marvel Database (episode and Adrian Toomes (Earth-92131)) and the Marvel Animated wiki name it Toomes Aerodynamics. Wikipedia's summary says 'Toomes Aeronautical', and I found no transcript to settle the name.
